Exists: IMSLP 'Cantabile e valser' (aliases 'Cantabile e valtz'), Op. 19 / MS 45, E major, violin & guitar (Wikipedia: MS 45). First edition is for violin & piano (Universal Edition 1922, ed. Title/key OK. Number conflict: IMSLP page is titled 'MS 63', but Ricordi (ed. Vescovo) and Wikipedia's MS list give MS 68 (MS 63 is the Rondo for violin & cello). Keep MS 68. Editions: Ricordi (Vescovo), Zanibon 1978 (ed. Bulatoff).

verdicts.title: Sonata a violino principale in A major
verdicts.note: Exists: IMSLP 'Sonata a violino principale con accomp. di violino e violoncello (o di piano), Oeuvres posthumes', A major, Schott c.1850 (plate 17530), Ranzato (Trieste 1927), Fritz Meyer (Schott), SHV Praha 1963 ('Tema con variazioni'); Wikipedia lists it among works without MS number. Title uses 'a violino principale', not 'per'. IMSLP also calls it 'Sonata No.10' (unexplained); no recording found. Original accompaniment is violin + cello (piano alternative).

Title OK. Sonata Varsavia, MS 57 (1828/29), variations on a mazurka by Elsner; only the solo part survives, completed by Pietro Spada (Boccaccini & Spada BS1270, vln/pno); Dacci piano realisation earlier. Recorded by Accardo (EMI), Kremer/Muti (Philips), Irnberger. Duration ~15-16 min, not 12.

Title OK (optionally add '(on G string)'; E-flat major sounding, G string tuned up to B-flat). MS 51, 1828, variations on Haydn's Austrian hymn; ~15 min; Boccaccini & Spada 1994 (BS1291, ed. Bolognese); recorded by Accardo/Dutoit (DG), Hossen (Dynamic).
Listed in Wikipedia's MS catalogue (MS 46, Sonata militare, 'Non piu andrai', c.1818-24) but no published edition and no recording found in several searches; treat as unpublished.

verdicts.title: Polacca con variazioni in A major, MS 18
verdicts.note: Exists: MS 18, A major, violin & orchestra (before 1810); edition P. Spada (Presser/Boccaccini & Spada, vln/pno); recorded by Accardo (EMI, ~7:51) and Milenkovich (vln/pno, 7:45). Catalogue number confirmed (MS 18); duration ~8 min.

Second arrangement of Caprice No. 24 (Kreisler's version, N50, is the one with a commercial recording, Naxos 8570703). Auer's edition exists (Carl Fischer 1922, ed. Saenger, adds own variations) but no recording found; keep only one.

Kreisler's violin & piano arrangement of Caprice No. 24: Charles Foley (Carl Fischer) 1913 (IMSLP, Wikipedia Kreisler list); recorded by Philippe Quint/Dmitriy Cogan, Naxos 8570703 (with Nos. 13 and 20).

Kreisler's own title is 'Concerto in one movement' (rescored/condensed first movement of Op. 6, with his cadenza); Foley/Carl Fischer edition; recorded by Kreisler/Ormandy (Victor 1936), Korcia (2014), ~16 min.
